title: TwoFactorSetup
wrapsNative: MonarchDialog with a close button and Cancel and Next actions over three steps: an optional androidx.compose.foundation.Image of a QR code the app draws and MonarchCopyField for the setup key; MonarchOtpPinInput; MonarchRecoveryCodes
summary: A recipe, not a component: a dialog that turns on two-step verification in three steps: scan a QR code or enter a key in an authenticator app, enter a code from it, and save the recovery codes.
whenToUse: In account security settings, when a person turns on two-step verification with an authenticator app.
whenNotToUse: To ask for a code at sign-in, use MonarchOtpPinInput alone. To re-confirm a signed-in person, use MonarchStepUpAuthDialog.
api: MonarchDialog(onDismissRequest = { open = false }, title = title, description = description, closeButton = true, actions = { Cancel and Next }, content = { … })
Image(painter = qrCode, contentDescription = "QR code for the authenticator app") — qrCode drawn by the app
MonarchOtpPinInput(value = code, onValueChange = …, label = "6-digit code", errorText = codeError)

options.name: secret / account
options.description: The shared key from the server and the name of the account it belongs to, shown under the QR code.

options.name: qrCode
options.description: A QR code of the otpauth address for scanning, drawn by the app's own generator. Without it only the key is shown.

options.name: step
options.description: The current step, kept with rememberSaveable. The dialog title and the Next button follow it.

states.name: scan
states.description: The QR code when the app provides one, the account, and the setup key with a copy button.

states.name: verify
states.description: A six-cell code field; an incomplete or rejected code shows the field's error.

states.name: recovery
states.description: The recovery codes with copy, save or share, and the "I have saved my recovery codes" acknowledgement, which finishes the setup.

appearance: Existing Monarch components in the theme: the dialog's title, description and footer actions, the copy field's monospaced key, the code cells and the recovery codes panel. A QR code must stay dark on light in every theme so scanners can read it; draw it that way in the app.
platformNotes: The web's TwoFactorSetup is a dialog with a QR code as its first step, and so is this recipe: a centred MonarchDialog with a close button, a step count, Cancel and Next. iOS draws the QR code with Core Image; Android has no first-party QR generator and Monarch adds no dependency, so the recipe shows an app-supplied Painter when there is one (for example from ZXing in the app); the setup key stays as the fallback for entering it in the app by hand.
accessibility: The dialog is named by its title, which follows the step, and the step count is read with it.
The key is copied with a button and spelled out by the copy field; the QR image has a description when shown.
The code field reads its error.
Recovery codes are read character by character, and a missing acknowledgement is announced.
edgeCases: Without a QR painter the step shows the key alone.
Long keys wrap in the copy field; the code field accepts the keyboard's one-time code suggestion.
